## eBird status and trends

Resources:

- Data: [Download Data Products - eBird Science](https://science.ebird.org/en/status-and-trends/download-data)
- R package: [Access and Analyze eBird Status and Trends Data Products • ebirdst](https://ebird.github.io/ebirdst/index.html)

Example:

- [Common Tern Range Map, All About Birds, Cornell Lab of Ornithology](https://www.allaboutbirds.org/guide/Common_Tern/maps-range)
- [Common Tern - Abundance Map - eBird Status and Trends](https://science.ebird.org/en/status-and-trends/species/comter/abundance-map)


Code from Tim (using Gemini)...

```{r}
# Install the package directly from GitHub if you haven't already
# remotes::install_github("ebird/ebirdst")

library(ebirdst)
library(terra)
library(sf)

# 1. Set your access key (request this for free at ebird.org/st/request)
# This saves the key to your .Renviron file
ebird_key_txt <- "~/My Drive/private/2026-08-19_eBird.org_status-and-trends-key_ben@oceanmetrics.io.txt"
ebird_key <- readLines(ebird_key_txt)
# set_ebirdst_access_key(ebird_key)

# 2. Download the Common Tern data package (Species code: "comter")
# This caches the files locally in your designated data directory so you only run it once.
ebirdst_download_status(species = "comter")
# ebirdst_data_dir() # "/Users/bbest/Library/Application Support/org.R-project.R/R/ebirdst"

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# OPTION A: The Range Polygons (Vector)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Load the seasonal boundaries as an sf object to use as a geographic bounding box
tern_ranges <- load_ranges(
  species = "comter",
  resolution = "27km",
  smoothed = TRUE
)

# Plot to verify the seasonal polygons (Breeding, Non-breeding, Passage)
plot(tern_ranges["season"], main = "Common Tern: Seasonal Extent of Occurrence")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# OPTION B: The Predictive Heatmaps (Raster Cube)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Load the 52-week relative abundance GeoTIFFs as a terra SpatRaster stack
tern_abundance <- load_raster(
  species = "comter",
  product = "abundance",
  period = "weekly",
  resolution = "27km" # Change to "3km" for the native, unaggregated high-resolution scale
)

# Plot a single layer (e.g., Week 20 for mid-spring migration) to visualize the density gradient
plot(tern_abundance[[20]], main = "Common Tern: Relative Abundance - Week 20")
```
